channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 speech models and voice agent SDK
item.description: Mistral AI released Voxtral 3, a family of speech-to-text and text-to-speech models alongside a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit. The system combines transcription, reasoning, and speech output into a streaming pipeline with sub-one-second turn latency priced at $0.04 per minute. Voxtral 3 integrates the full voice agent stack into a single pipeline, offering European-hosted and self-deployed alternatives to providers like OpenAI and ElevenLabs.

item.title: Mistral launches public preview of Mistral Large 4
item.description: Mistral has launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters. The preview API is available on Mistral Studio, with weights releasing at the end of the month. Mistral Large 4 represents a major European-built open-weight release intended to compete with global frontier models while offering self-deployment and control under European law.

item.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini open-weights model
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter open-weights Mixture-of-Experts transformer that loops its middle layers three times per token. The ~20GB model is small enough to run on consumer laptops and leads open-weights models under 100B parameters on benchmarks like DeepSWE v1.1. The release demonstrates the practical application of looped transformer architectures in sub-100B parameter models designed for local hardware execution.

item.title: Researcher tests AI supply chain with 2 million canaries and finds data leaks
item.description: Security researcher HD Moore planted nearly 2 million trackable secrets in prompts sent through AI services to test for data leakage between July and November 2026. The experiment uncovered compromised AI providers, prompt logging by resellers, and ignored privacy settings. The findings demonstrate that sensitive data sent to AI applications can leak through routers, resellers, and compromised hosting providers despite encryption in transit.

item.title: Trump threatens tax and ban on US companies building data centers overseas
item.description: President Donald Trump stated that U.S. companies will be blocked from building data centers overseas or face a heavy tax. Major cloud providers including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle have already built data centers in other countries. The proposal addresses the geopolitical and energy constraints of the AI boom, forcing a clash between domestic infrastructure policy and the global expansion strategies of major tech companies.

item.title: METR updates AI time horizon report with harder tasks and judgment focus
item.description: Nonprofit evaluation group METR released an update to its time horizon report, finding that while frontier AI models continue rapid capability gains on verifiable tasks like coding, their performance lags on open-ended tasks requiring judgment. The updated TH2 suite tests models on 36 tasks across 12 families, showing that time horizons double roughly every 110 days. Understanding the capability gap between verifiable coding tasks and open-ended research judgment is critical for assessing progress toward automated AI R&D.

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved Riemann hypothesis with Claude
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published a claim that he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old open mathematical problem. The solution has not yet been independently verified by experts or accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute. If verified by the mathematics community, it would represent a major milestone for AI in solving long-standing open problems in number theory.

item.title: Levent Alpöge reports discovering proof of Riemann Hypothesis with Claude
item.description: Mathematician Levent Alpöge stated that he discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis while working with Anthropic's Claude model. According to the report, the AI model also helped formalize the arguments without assumptions. This account highlights an instance of an AI assistant being used to tackle and potentially resolve long-standing mathematical problems.

item.title: Anthropic Nasdaq debut sparks buying rush among Indian retail investors
item.description: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut drove heavy trading activity among Indian retail investors across overseas platforms including INDmoney, Mudrex, and Vested. The company accounted for 40% of INDmoney's international investment activity and 11% of total traded value on Vested on its listing day. The surge in retail trading activity demonstrates how public listings by major AI companies create new entry points for everyday investors seeking exposure to artificial intelligence developers outside of venture capital.

item.title: OpenAI reportedly developing first smartphone with Foxconn subsidiary assembly
item.description: OpenAI is reportedly developing its first smartphone, with Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile securing assembly orders for a potential launch in late 2027 or 2028. Neither OpenAI nor Foxconn has officially confirmed the project. This reported hardware project marks a potential expansion by OpenAI beyond software into consumer devices, putting it in possible competition with major handset manufacturers.

item.title: Pragmatik Labs reaches $5 billion valuation in new funding round
item.description: Shanghai-based Pragmatik Labs raised tens of millions of dollars in funding. The startup was founded by former Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. AI chief Junyang Lin and reached a $5 billion valuation, up from $2 billion in August. The funding round highlights significant capital movement in the AI startup sector, specifically regarding companies founded by former major tech executives.

item.title: SatSure raises ₹60 Cr from Antariksh VC fund in Series B round
item.description: Earth-intelligence startup SatSure has raised ₹60 Cr from the state-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund in the first tranche of its ₹200 Cr Series B round at an ₹870 Cr valuation. The capital will advance optical payloads built by its subsidiary KaleidEO, scale its geospatial AI model Dhaarini, and expand international operations. This investment marks the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund's first entry into the downstream data and AI layer of India's commercial space economy.

item.title: Architect Labs unveils AI-designed Frostbite CPU architecture
item.description: US AI startup Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU architecture designed and verified by AI. The company claims the design delivers 4.59 times the performance per watt and 8.77 times the performance per area compared to a conventional CPU core across 25 workloads in pre-silicon simulations. This release represents an attempt to use autonomous AI systems for co-designing software and hardware across the stack, potentially bypassing decades of human-made CPU design stagnation.

item.title: OpenAI details methods to combat adversarial distillation and protect reasoning
item.description: OpenAI published details on how it detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, a process where bad actors use frontier model outputs without authorization to train models without safeguards. The company reported that updated defenses in GPT-6.2 Astra lowered the average attack success rate for recovering protected reasoning from 54.0% to 0.2%. Preventing adversarial distillation helps stop bad actors from reproducing advanced model capabilities, such as in cybersecurity and biology, without appropriate safety protections.

item.title: Analysis of 10M job ads in China shows double-digit decline for AI-exposed roles
item.description: An analysis of 10 million job advertisements in China between 2021 and 2025 revealed a double-digit decline in listings for roles with high AI exposure compared to less-exposed positions. The study highlights a growing impact of artificial intelligence on hiring trends in the region. It provides empirical data on how AI adoption affects hiring demand across different job categories over a four-year period.

item.title: Signal restricts screenshots to block AI agents from reading messages
item.description: Encrypted messaging service Signal introduced default restrictions on screenshots to prevent device-level AI agents from reading private chats. The company warned that operating system integrations by tech giants pose an existential threat to its privacy guarantee. The move highlights the direct conflict between operating system-level AI assistants that scan screens for context and privacy-focused end-to-end encrypted applications.

item.title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
item.description: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models on their websites. The plan, discussed by the Treasury Department and the White House, aims to discourage reliance on Chinese AI without imposing outright restrictions. This proposal signals an emerging policy shift to counter the adoption of Chinese open-weight AI models by US businesses through public pressure rather than direct bans.

item.title: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq at $1.5 trillion valuation after $81.34 billion IPO
item.description: Anthropic went public on Nasdaq after raising USD 81.34 billion in an initial public offering that valued the company at approximately USD 1.5 trillion. CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company will prioritize safety and human control over business or political pressures. This major public market debut tests whether a leading AI lab can maintain its stated focus on safety and slower deployment schedules after achieving a multi-trillion-dollar valuation.

item.title: Nscale may need US license for ByteDance GPU access under new rules
item.description: Nscale must seek a US license to continue providing ByteDance remote access to Nvidia GPUs under new export regulations. ByteDance accounted for approximately 73% of Nscale's 2025 revenue. This highlights how tighter US export rules targeting computing capacity in third countries impact infrastructure providers with ties to Chinese companies.

item.title: Asian tech stocks plunge as Anthropic IPO fails to stem AI sell-off
item.description: Asian technology stocks dropped following Anthropic's $81.3 billion initial public offering as the record listing failed to halt a wider artificial intelligence stock sell-off. SoftBank shares fell 14.67%, while Japanese stocks lost over JPY 53 trillion. The market reaction highlights how massive capital concentration in high-profile AI offerings can coincide with broader pullbacks across tech equities.

item.title: Ethan Mollick highlights research on 35 human labs deploying science agents
item.description: Ethan Mollick highlighted research where 35 human labs deployed agents that collaborated to conduct science, publishing 936 papers. The agents also publicly retracted mistakes, published null results more than humans, and founded a peer review journal. It demonstrates an early model of how multi-agent systems can autonomously conduct, publish, and review scientific research.

item.title: Anthropic shares slide 5% in after-hours trading following record IPO
item.description: Anthropic shares fell more than 5% in after-hours trading, slipping below its IPO level following a record $107.3 billion initial public offering. The decline occurred amid a broad market selloff driven by investor doubts regarding artificial intelligence profitability and high spending. For those following AI, the market reaction highlights growing skepticism over whether heavy capital expenditures in artificial intelligence will translate into sustainable business returns.

item.title: Google selects Blue Origin to launch Project Suncatcher AI satellites in 2029
item.description: Google selected Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, an experiment testing AI computing in space. The mission is targeted for the first quarter of 2029. The initiative explores moving power-hungry AI workloads into orbit to bypass ground-based electricity and cooling constraints.

item.title: SpaceXSI denies liability in UK lawmaker's lawsuit over Grok images
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceXSI filed a defense against a lawsuit brought by British lawmaker Jess Asato over sexualised AI images generated by Grok. The company argued that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach privacy rights. This is one of the first legal claims testing platform liability for the design of an AI system and how developers contest privacy lawsuits.

item.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over former CEO Jensen Huang's affair
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia on Thursday to investigate whether former CEO Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information. The probe also examines whether the company misled investors and the public regarding the risks. The investigation marks a significant legal escalation for Nvidia as state and federal regulators intensify scrutiny over the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's departure and export control compliance.

item.title: US Commerce Dept approved sales of over 879K AI chips to Chinese companies
item.description: The US Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies as of May 2026, according to disclosures released by House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast. The approvals included entities on the Department of Defense's Chinese military-linked list. This disclosure highlights the scale of US-approved AI chip sales to Chinese entities, including those linked to the military, amid scrutiny over export controls.

item.title: ChatPRD ends free trials after facing widespread token fraud abuse
item.description: ChatPRD founder Claire Vo reports that groups are abusing free trials to steal and resell AI tokens or run commercial enterprises. The widespread fraud has forced ChatPRD to wind down its free trials entirely. The rise of organized token fraud highlights the growing vulnerability of AI platforms to systematic abuse of promotional offerings.

item.title: Mistral opens Singapore headquarters and targets 200 Asia-Pacific staff by 2027
item.description: French artificial intelligence company Mistral opened its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore on November 20, 2026, aiming to double its regional headcount to 200 people by 2027. The office will focus on public sector agencies, high-tech manufacturing, and robotics. The expansion establishes a European AI provider with a physical research and engineering presence in Southeast Asia, where Chinese open-weight models are already widely used.

item.title: Google DeepMind institute outlines four pathways from AGI to ASI
item.description: Google DeepMind researchers published an essay outlining four pathways for AI development to move from human-level AGI to artificial general superintelligence (ASI). The essay notes that global effective compute has grown at least tenfold per year. For people following AI research, this framework maps out theoretical and technical pathways beyond human-level AGI toward superintelligence, alongside constraints and compute growth trends.

item.title: Anthropic raises $81.3B in record-breaking IPO as founders cash out $2B
item.description: Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising $81.3 billion in an initial public offering that included $1.95 billion for its seven founders. The stock closed at $97.17 per share, giving the company a valuation of roughly $1.7 trillion. The offering marks one of the largest public debuts in history, significantly expanding the capital and corporate backing available to a major AI lab while creating thousands of millionaire employees.
